Downsample to fixed time bins

Source: R/process.R
g3_downsample.Rd

Averages samples within bins of fixed width, for example to reduce 50 Hz data to 100 ms bins before fitting a generalised additive mixed model. Fewer samples make models faster to fit and reduce the autocorrelation the model has to account for.

Usage

g3_downsample(x, bin = 0.1, min_valid = 0.5, by = NULL)

Arguments

x

Gaze data from read_g3_gaze(), epochs from g3_epochs() or long pupil data from g3_pupil_long().

bin

Bin width in seconds.

min_valid

Proportion of samples in a bin that must have a value. A numeric column is NA in bins where fewer of its samples are available, so that bins mostly lost to a blink do not get a value from the few samples left.

by

Names of further columns to group by, such as a participant or condition column. They are kept in the result.

Value

A tibble with one row per bin and group, starting with the grouping columns. samples gives the number of samples in the bin. A pulse column gets the pulse of the first sample in the bin. Other numeric columns hold the mean of the available samples, and logical columns, such as valid, the proportion of TRUE samples. All other columns are dropped. A grouped tibble keeps its groups.

Details

Bins are counted from time 0, or from the onset for epochs from g3_epochs(), so that the onset falls on a bin boundary. Each bin is labelled with its start time. Rows are grouped by the recording, epoch and eye columns where these exist, so the function works on the output of read_g3_gaze(), g3_add_syncport(), g3_epochs() and g3_pupil_long(). Columns named in by are added to these groups, and so are the groups of a grouped tibble.

Examples

gaze <- read_g3_gaze(g3_example())
g3_downsample(gaze, bin = 0.1)
#> # A tibble: 300 × 25
#>    recording  time samples gaze2d_x gaze2d_y gaze3d_x gaze3d_y gaze3d_z
#>    <chr>     <dbl>   <int>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl>
#>  1 recording   0         5    0.452    0.857     69.7    -264.     660.
#>  2 recording   0.1       5    0.449    0.867    230.     -871.    2130.
#>  3 recording   0.2       5    0.455    0.870    371.    -1522.    3725.
#>  4 recording   0.3       5    0.454    0.895     57.4    -254.     579.
#>  5 recording   0.4       5    0.451    0.906     42.3    -181.     400.
#>  6 recording   0.5       5    0.380    0.742    425.     -380.    1611.
#>  7 recording   0.6       5    0.374    0.654    548.     -326.    2019.
#>  8 recording   0.7       5    0.372    0.658    553.     -335.    1997.
#>  9 recording   0.8       5    0.369    0.668    563.     -357.    1990.
#> 10 recording   0.9       5    0.363    0.670    887.     -551.    3025.
#> # ℹ 290 more rows
#> # ℹ 17 more variables: left_origin_x <dbl>, left_origin_y <dbl>,
#> #   left_origin_z <dbl>, left_direction_x <dbl>, left_direction_y <dbl>,
#> #   left_direction_z <dbl>, left_pupil <dbl>, right_origin_x <dbl>,
#> #   right_origin_y <dbl>, right_origin_z <dbl>, right_direction_x <dbl>,
#> #   right_direction_y <dbl>, right_direction_z <dbl>, right_pupil <dbl>,
#> #   valid_left <dbl>, valid_right <dbl>, valid <dbl>

rec <- read_g3(g3_example())
ep <- g3_epochs(rec$gaze, rec$events, before = 0.5, after = 3, direction = "out")
g3_downsample(g3_pupil_long(ep), bin = 0.1)
#> # A tibble: 342 × 14
#>    recording epoch eye   epoch_time samples   time gaze2d_x gaze2d_y gaze3d_x

  dplyr::mutate(participant = "P01") |>
  g3_downsample(bin = 0.1, by = "participant")
